items.headline: Microsoft and Anthropic make up 85% of Nscale's $103 billion IPO backlog
items.why: It shows how much of the AI-infrastructure boom's headline value rests on a two-customer book with barely $3 billion of contracts actually live, a risk public investors will now be asked to underwrite.

items.headline: SoftBank launches $11 billion bond sale to fund its next OpenAI payment
items.why: AI capital needs are now large enough to reshape how one of the industry's biggest backers finances itself, pulling frontier-model funding directly into global credit markets.

items.headline: AMD briefly tops a $1 trillion market cap as the AI chip trade broadens
items.why: Investors are pricing AI infrastructure as a multi-winner semiconductor cycle rather than a single-supplier story, spreading risk and reward beyond Nvidia.

items.headline: Ireland fines Google €403 million over historical location-data practices
items.why: The penalty confirms that past data-collection practices keep generating major regulatory liability for large platforms years after the products themselves changed.

items.headline: Amazon blocks Meta's Muse AI agent from shopping on Amazon.com
items.why: The standoff signals a coming fight over who controls product discovery and the customer relationship as AI agents start shopping on people's behalf.

items.headline: Bitcoin surges to an 8-month high near $85,134
items.why: The move, driven by falling oil prices and a squeeze on short sellers, shows crypto decoupling from the regulatory setback of the CLARITY Act's Senate failure.

items.headline: Ethereum climbs alongside bitcoin to $2,713.90, up roughly 7% on the week
items.why: Ether tracking bitcoin's rally in lockstep suggests the move is a broad risk-on shift in crypto rather than an asset-specific catalyst.

items.headline: Crypto held its footing through the Fed's September 16 rate hike
items.why: Bitcoin and ethereum absorbing the first Fed hike in three years without a sustained selloff suggests crypto is trading more on liquidity and oil-price signals than on rate-path headlines.

items.headline: Bitcoin and ethereum are still up 21.2% and 28.9% on the month despite the volatility
items.why: The scale of the monthly gain shows this week's swings are noise on top of a genuine trend move, not a reversal of it.

items.headline: The Fed raised rates to 3.75%-4.00%, its first hike in three years
items.why: A unanimous vote under new Chair Kevin Warsh, with markets now pricing another hike this year, signals the Fed has firmly pivoted from cutting to fighting oil-driven inflation.

items.headline: Saudi-Houthi fighting spreads toward the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz, and Iran hit a tanker attempting the strait
items.why: With Iran's Revolutionary Guard confirming it struck a tanker for an 'illegal passage' through Hormuz, the conflict is now directly threatening the route that carries roughly a fifth of global oil and LNG.

items.headline: Trump hosts Xi in Washington this week for talks on trade, Taiwan and rare earths
items.why: China's one-year suspension of rare-earth export controls expires November 10, giving Beijing real leverage in a summit both sides are framing as unlikely to produce major breakthroughs.

sources.title: Trump set for Washington summit with Xi focused on trade, Taiwan and AI

items.headline: The Bank of Japan also raised rates, to a 31-year high
items.why: Simultaneous tightening from the Fed and BOJ shows the current inflation problem, driven largely by energy prices, is now a coordinated global central-bank concern rather than a US-only issue.

items.headline: Gold notched its first weekly gain in four, testing resistance near $4,400-$4,440
items.why: Gold holding up despite the Fed's rate hike and a stronger dollar suggests inflation-hedge demand is outweighing the usual headwind from higher yields.

items.headline: Brent and WTI both fell back below $100 a barrel, down 4.3% and 2.9% on the week
items.why: Oil giving back its early-week spike eased inflation pressure just as the Fed was raising rates, feeding directly into gold's and crypto's rebounds later in the week.

items.headline: Copper led base metals higher, up 3.0% to $6.63 a pound, while lithium fell 5.6%
items.why: The split between rising copper and falling lithium points to diverging demand stories: grid and AI-infrastructure buildout versus a still-soft EV-battery market.

items.headline: Silver outperformed gold, up 2.7% to $66.24 an ounce
items.why: Silver's larger percentage move than gold's is a classic signal of risk-on positioning returning to precious metals rather than pure safe-haven demand.

items.headline: S&P 500 stayed below wedge support, briefly broke flag support on the Fed decision, then reclaimed it
items.why: The index holding the 0.5-0.618 Fibonacci retracement and reclaiming flag support on the bounce keeps the bull case alive, but a break below the 7,500 area and last week's low would open a retest of the late-July low.

items.headline: Gold is testing the $4,400-$4,440 resistance band that has capped it since mid-September
items.why: A clean move above that band would clear the way for gold's next leg higher; failure there keeps it range-bound below the recent highs.
